title: Artificial Intelligence Based Rating of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome Efficacy in Clinical Diagnosis
authors: Elif Sarıca Darol, Yıldız Ece, Süleyman Uzun, Murat Alemdar
abstract: Evaluates SVM, Ensemble, Decision Tree, and KNN for 4-class CTS severity grading (Normal n=157, Mild n=92, Moderate n=55, Severe n=11; Padua scale) on 315 patients at Sakarya Training and Research Hospital using 17 demographic and Median/Ulnar NCS parameters.
source_excerpt: SVM achieved 93.55% accuracy, 95.75% precision, 92.22% sensitivity, 97.20% specificity, 93.69% F1-score, and 0.94 AUC on a 10% hold-out test split (n=31), followed by Ensemble (80.65% accuracy, 0.88 AUC), Decision Tree (70.97%), and KNN (64.52%). Limitations: Padua severity grade is deterministically defined by the same NCS thresholds fed as input features (circular label leakage); only 11 severe cases in total (1 in test set).

title: Application of Machine Learning Algorithms for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
authors: Yıldız Yener, Elif Sarıca Darol, Süleyman Uzun, Murat Alemdar, Tuncay Çolak
venue: Journal of the Anatomical Society of India, 73(2), 178-183
abstract: Applies SVM, Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, and KNN to the same 315-patient Sakarya University ENMG cohort (17 demographic and Median/Ulnar motor-sensory NCS features) reformulated for binary CTS vs. non-CTS classification (80% train n=251, 20% test n=64).
source_excerpt: SVM achieved 96% accuracy (0.96 precision, 0.96 sensitivity, 0.96 specificity, 0.96 F1, 0.99 AUC; 31/32 TN, 31/32 TP), outperforming Logistic Regression (93% accuracy, 0.98 AUC), Naive Bayes (92% accuracy, 0.97 AUC), and KNN (92% accuracy, 0.96 AUC). Limitations: Re-uses the Darol et al. (2023) 315-patient cohort without cross-validation and exhibits circular NCS ground-truth leakage.

title: Automatic Electrodiagnosis of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome Using Machine Learning
authors: Konstantinos I. Tsamis, Prokopis Kontogiannis, Ioannis Gourgiotis, Stefanos Ntabos, Ioannis Sarmas, George Manis
local_pdf_path: papers/Automatic Electrodiagnosis of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome Using.pdf
abstract: Prospective study of 65 hands (38 subjects: 19 control, 10 mild, 17 moderate, 19 severe) extracting 302 NCS waveform features per hand (11 common + 23 novel physiological/geometric features across 8 motor/sensory nerves plus 30 cross-nerve differences) with two-stage SBS+SFS feature selection and LOOCV.
source_excerpt: Combining common and novel waveform features (expanded area, half-max duration, subarea ratios, onset/offset tangent slopes reflecting axonal repolarization) with SVM achieved 96.92% accuracy (2-class vs NCS), 89.06% (2-class vs clinical diagnosis, where novel features alone at 87.48% beat common features at 86.91%), 94.15% (3-class vs NCS), 72.73% (3-class vs clinical using DT on novel features), and 91.17% (4-class vs NCS).

title: Carpal tunnel syndrome prediction with machine learning algorithms using anthropometric and strength-based measurement
authors: Mehmet Yetiş, Hikmet Kocaman, Mehmet Canlı, Hasan Yıldırım, Aysu Yetiş, İsmail Ceylan
abstract: Case-control study (N=112: 56 bilateral CTS patients + 56 healthy controls) predicting CTS from 13 non-invasive anthropometric and grip/pinch strength measurements (65:35 train/test split, n=38 test).
source_excerpt: Random Forests (mtry=4) achieved 89.474% test accuracy, F1=0.905, Kappa=0.789 (TP=19, FP=4, FN=0, TN=15; 100% sensitivity, 78.9% specificity), followed by XGBoost Linear (86.842% accuracy, F1=0.878, Kappa=0.736), MLP (78.947%), SVM-Poly (76.316%), and SVM-Radial (73.684%). Top features: Wrist Circumference, Hand Width, Hand Grip Strength, Tip Pinch, Key Pinch, Middle Finger Length.

title: Machine learning-based approach for disease severity classification of carpal tunnel syndrome
authors: Dougho Park, Byung Hee Kim, Sang-Eok Lee, Dong Young Kim, Mansu Kim, Heum Dai Kwon, Mun-Chul Kim, Ae Ryoung Kim, Hyoung Seop Kim, Jang Woo Lee
local_pdf_path: papers/Machine learning‑based approach for disease severity classification.pdf
abstract: Retrospective study of 1,037 CTS hands (507 mild, 276 moderate, 254 severe by Stevens electrodiagnostic grading) classified using 11 clinical + sonographic variables (NRS pain, BMI, duration, nocturnal pain, thenar atrophy, ultrasound CSA, and Palmar Bowing PB) on a 70:30 split (n=274 test hands).
source_excerpt: In 3-class multi-class classification, XGBoost achieved 76.6% test accuracy (95% CI 71.2-81.5%) and Random Forest achieved 75.6%, with a pronounced bottleneck on Moderate grade (71.8% balanced accuracy vs 83.6% Mild and 83.5% Severe). OvR stacked ensemble with SMOTE improved Severe-vs-Rest to 90.9% accuracy (ROC 0.95) and Mild-vs-Rest to 83.6% (ROC 0.86), while Moderate-vs-Rest remained at 78.8% (ROC 0.81, sensitivity 60.0%). Palmar Bowing ranked higher in feature importance than CSA.

title: One-Stop Automated Diagnostic System for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome in Ultrasound Images Using Deep Learning
abstract: Presents OSA-CTSD on 32,301 2D wrist ultrasound frames from 130 continuous sweep videos (81 subjects: 90 healthy wrists, 40 CTS wrists; 8:1:1 patient-level split), combining SegFormer-B2 segmentation, automated biometric computation, and explainable Random Forest classification.
source_excerpt: SegFormer-B2 (24.73M params, 47.28 FPS) achieved Dice 85.78±8.71%, IoU 76.00±11.98%, HD95 7.21±4.74 px, ASSD 2.64±1.52 px. Frame-level MAE: CSA 1.71±0.80 mm², Perimeter 1.41±0.44 mm, AD 0.20±0.09 mm. RF classifier achieved 93.85% accuracy, 85.00% sensitivity, 97.78% specificity, 89.47% F1, and 0.98 AUC (outperforming inexperienced radiologists at 90.26% acc and matching experienced radiologists at 98.21%, p=0.08). Swelling Ratio (SR) contributed 42.9% feature importance (0.96 single-feature AUC), while Max Flattening Ratio (FR) contributed only 0.6% (0.57 AUC).

title: CaRing: Preventing Carpal Tunnel Syndrome based on Daily Activities from Always-Available Input Device
authors: CP Li, RH Liang, H Dong
abstract: Index-finger base-knuckle wearable ring with ADNS-9800 laser optical flow sensor at 5° orientation (12 Hz sampling) and session-relative 30% first-step threshold for continuous mouse usage monitoring and CTS prevention.
source_excerpt: Across 35 recordings (138,053 samples, 3.2 hours) and a 10-user study, CaRing detected ~90% of mouse start/end events within 2s (3% late, 7% missed), accommodated a 12x inter-user variation in first-step plateau height (15 to 179 counts, median 44), and showed users underestimate their mouse usage duration by 1.4x (9 min self-reported vs 13 min recorded, Wilcoxon W=1.5, p=0.006).

title: Evaluating Deep Learning-Based Nerve Segmentation in Brachial Plexus Ultrasound Under Realistic Data Constraints
abstract: Evaluates 5-fold GroupKFold U-Net nerve segmentation across 3 seeds on 955 UBPD images split by scanner domain: Ultrasound-1 (594 images, 52 patients, Siemens ACUSON NX3 Elite) and Ultrasound-2 (361 images, 36 patients, Philips EPIQ5).
source_excerpt: Binary nerve Dice was 0.274±0.087 on U1, 0.407±0.124 on U2, and 0.388±0.094 on Combined U1+U2 (+0.114 regularization gain over U1). Naive 4-class segmentation (artery, vein, nerve, muscle) severely degraded nerve Dice by -61% on U1 (to 0.107), -11% on U2 (to 0.363), and -9% on Combined (to 0.355). Nerve mask pixel area correlated positively with Dice (Pearson r=0.587, p=9.0e-6).
